solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Very strong urge when one has black pocketed in pool (6)

indicators.note: what is pocketed sits inside the pool
the one holds the black beside it, so B and I travel together

blocks.note: a lido is an open-air swimming pool
B = black, as on pencils
I = one, the Roman numeral

annotation.surface: A snooker player aches to sink the black in a pool game.
annotation.walkthrough: Pool and black suggest the table game, but the pool here is a lido, an open-air swimming pool, and the black ball is just the letter B.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym at the intense end: the psychological term for sexual desire, the drive Freud treated as the strongest of urges.

entries.clue: The short right disposed of bully (8)

indicators.note: a short THE is missing its last letter

blocks.note: THE cut short
R = right
food eaten has been disposed of

annotation.surface: The political right has got rid of a bully.
annotation.walkthrough: Read 'bully' as a noun and the clue seems to be about getting rid of a tyrant; it is a verb, and 'disposed of' means finished off at the table.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: intimidating someone with menaces is both bullying and threatening.

entries.clue: Be in strong position – as will dealer? (4,3,3,5)

blocks.note: the idiom for having every advantage
literally, a card dealer holds the whole pack before dealing

annotation.surface: Someone in command of a situation is compared to a card dealer.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half takes the idiom literally: before the deal, the dealer really does hold every card. The question mark flags that playful reading.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for having every advantage, and literally true of the dealer, who has the whole pack in hand before dealing.

entries.clue: Law, work of art impressing unionist in the end (7)

indicators.note: to impress is to press into, so the statue takes the T inside it
take only the final letter of unionist

blocks.note: a statue is a work of art
last letter of unionisT

annotation.surface: A piece of public art makes an impression on a unionist politician.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unionist' looks like a political clue, but only its final T is used.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an act passed by a legislature, the written kind of law as opposed to custom.

entries.clue: Lessening bloom, wallflower (9,6)

blocks.note: shrinking = lessening
a violet is a flower

annotation.surface: A garden flower is wilting and getting smaller.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wallflower' is also a real plant, so the whole clue reads as horticulture; here it means a shy person at a party.
annotation.definitionFit: A shrinking violet is a very shy person, like a wallflower who stays at the edge of a dance.

entries.clue: Winger away with the fairies? (6)

blocks.note: a winged creature, here the bird
British idiom for being dreamy or a bit mad

annotation.surface: A footballer on the wing seems to be in a daydream.
annotation.walkthrough: A winger sounds like a footballer; it is anything with wings. 'Away with the fairies' is British slang for being dreamy or slightly mad.
annotation.definitionFit: A cuckoo is a bird, and cuckoo also means crazy.

entries.clue: Search vessel that’s under suspicion, initially (4)

indicators.note: in a down answer, what is under comes after
take the first letter of suspicion

blocks.note: first letter of Suspicion
a can is a container

annotation.surface: Police search a ship that is under suspicion.
annotation.walkthrough: The vessel looks like a ship being searched; it is a humble can, and 'that's under' places it below S in this down entry.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: running your eyes or a device over something to find what you want.

entries.clue: Serving of food is here in plate (4)

indicators.note: a serving is a portion, so take a portion of the words that follow

blocks.note: the answer runs from the last letter of food through is into the first letter of here

annotation.surface: A waiter announces that the food has arrived on the plate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Serving of food' looks like the definition, and DISH would fit it; the definition is the last word, and the serving is a slice of the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a shallow vessel for serving food, which the surface's serving of food hints at.

entries.clue: Frequently upper room won’t open (3)

indicators.note: the word loses its opening letter

blocks.note: a loft is a room at the top of a house

annotation.surface: The attic door is often stuck.
annotation.walkthrough: The stuck attic door is the picture; in the wordplay, LOFT simply loses its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Oft is an old word for often, frequently.

entries.clue: Feeling about a loin and leg (6)

indicators.note: the feeling goes about, around, the A

blocks.note: a hunch is an intuitive feeling
A as printed

annotation.surface: A butcher gets a sense of the meat on a joint.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Feeling' suggests touching the meat; it is a hunch.
annotation.definitionFit: A haunch of meat is the leg and loin together, as in a haunch of venison.

entries.clue: Information in offer for engine part (3,3)

indicators.note: the information goes inside the offer

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information
a bid is an offer

annotation.surface: A car seller gives details of an offer on a spare engine part.
annotation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information, as in 'the gen on something'.
annotation.definitionFit: The big end is the end of a connecting rod that fits round the crankshaft in an engine.

entries.clue: Fine piece for philosophy (8)

blocks.note: fine = thin, as in a fine thread
the king is a chess piece

annotation.surface: A splendid work suited to a philosophy course.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fine piece' reads as praise for a piece of writing; split it into thin and a chess piece.
annotation.definitionFit: A person's thinking is their philosophy, their way of seeing things.

entries.clue: Seek the violator out in aggressive business dealings (7,8)

definitions.note: plural in the clue; the answer is one such deal

indicators.note: out as in wrong, put out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 15 letters

annotation.surface: Hunt down the lawbreaker amid cut-throat business practices.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a manhunt; the three opening words are just letters to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A hostile takeover is a company buying another against its board's wishes, aggressive business indeed.

entries.clue: Corn in shaved goatee? (3)

indicators.note: shaving trims off the ends, here the first and last letters

blocks.note: a goatee is one kind of beard; the question mark flags the example
remove the outer letters B and D

annotation.surface: A grain of corn is stuck in a freshly trimmed goatee.
annotation.walkthrough: A goatee stands for BEARD by example, which the question mark admits.
annotation.definitionFit: An ear of corn is the seed-bearing head of the plant.

entries.clue: Service ending in prayer, shame originally unobserved (7)

indicators.note: the original, first, letter goes unseen

blocks.note: amen is the word that ends a prayer
PITY (a shame) without its first letter

annotation.surface: A church service finishes with prayer, and a disgrace passes unnoticed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Service' and 'prayer' paint a church scene, but the service is a facility; shame is pity, as in 'what a shame'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the facilities sense: a pool or a bus route is an amenity, a service laid on for residents.

entries.clue: Damage from sheep on the up (3)

indicators.note: in a down answer, going up means read bottom to top

blocks.note: a ram is a male sheep

annotation.surface: Harm done by a sheep that is climbing a hill.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'on the up' turns the word upside down.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb synonym, slightly literary: to spoil the look or quality of something.

entries.clue: European city, new part appearing shabby (7)

indicators.note: in poor shape, so the letters are knocked about

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: In a European city, even the new quarter looks run-down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'New' tempts you to use N and look for a word for part; the whole phrase 'new part' is the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Belgian port on the Scheldt is one of many European cities.

entries.clue: Endorsement of achievement anything but rare! (4,4)

blocks.note: said as praise
steak cooked through, the opposite of rare

annotation.surface: Praise for an accomplishment that is far from unusual.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rare' seems to mean unusual; it is the steak sense, whose opposite is well done.
annotation.definitionFit: "Well done!" praises an achievement; well-done meat is the opposite of rare.

entries.clue: Dodgy person keeping scrounging, ultimately? (7)

indicators.note: unreliable, so the letters of person are shaken up
the rearranged person keeps the G inside
take the last letter of scrounging

blocks.note: PERSON rearranged
last letter of scroungiNG

annotation.surface: A shady character who is always on the scrounge.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: read straight, it describes a sponger, a dodgy person always scrounging.
annotation.definitionFit: A sponger lives off others, a dodgy person always scrounging.

entries.clue: Where to go when out making Victorian pickle (7,8)

indicators.note: the answer is made out of the letters that follow

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 15 letters

annotation.surface: Advice on where to head once you have made an old-fashioned chutney.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pickle' looks like the mess that signals an anagram, but it is fodder. A batsman who is out walks back to the pavilion, the clubhouse at a cricket ground.
annotation.definitionFit: A dismissed batsman walks off to the cricket pavilion.

entries.clue: Very little money for policeman (6)

blocks.note: a penny or two-pence piece, the bronze coins of least value
British slang for a police officer

annotation.surface: A policeman is paid a pittance.
annotation.walkthrough: A copper is a low-value British coin, and also slang for a police officer.
annotation.definitionFit: Coppers are the smallest coins, and a copper is a policeman.

entries.clue: After content of box, reach for fruit (6)

indicators.note: the content is what sits in the middle of the word
'after' in its sense of following in sequence, so the reach is written after the box's content

blocks.note: middle letter of bOx
reach = range, as in the reach of a gun

annotation.surface: Having emptied a box, someone stretches for a piece of fruit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Content of box' looks like whatever the box holds; it is the letter at its centre.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the citrus is one fruit among many.

entries.clue: Member of the clergy fellow put down (8)

blocks.note: a chap is a fellow
lain = lying down, set down

annotation.surface: A clergyman's colleague is insulted.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put down' suggests an insult; it means laid down, LAIN.
annotation.definitionFit: A chaplain is a clergyman attached to a school, hospital or regiment.

entries.clue: Listen and hear everything every day, for starters (4)

indicators.note: take the first letter of each word

blocks.note: first letters of Hear Everything Every Day

annotation.surface: Advice to pay attention and take in everything, every day.
annotation.walkthrough: The advice reads naturally; only the first letters of the four words after 'and' count.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb synonym in the sense of paying attention: to listen to advice is to heed it.

entries.clue: Heavens opening in downpour, zero pick up coats (2,4)

indicators.note: the first letter of downpour
HEAR coats, wraps around, the D

blocks.note: O looks like zero
to pick up a sound is to hear it
first letter of Downpour

annotation.surface: The sky opens with a downpour and nobody picks up their coats.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heavens' and 'downpour' suggest the weather, but 'Heavens!' is an exclamation of dismay, like 'Oh dear!'.
annotation.definitionFit: "Heavens!" and "Oh dear!" are both mild exclamations of dismay.

entries.clue: Story say written in advance (6)

indicators.note: the EG is written into the middle of the other word

blocks.note: e.g. = for example, say
to lend money is to advance it

annotation.surface: A tale is set down in writing before it happens.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Written in advance' reads as prepared beforehand; split it, and 'written in' is the container instruction while 'advance' is a loan of money.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a traditional tale handed down, like those of King Arthur.

entries.clue: Sundown in the veldt (3)

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the last letter of the plus the first two of veldt

annotation.surface: Sunset over the South African grasslands.
annotation.walkthrough: The veldt is open grassland in southern Africa; the answer spans the gap between the two words.
annotation.definitionFit: Eve is an old word for evening, the time of sundown.

entries.clue: Return of hard liquor approaching (4)

indicators.note: the letters come back, reading right to left

blocks.note: H = hard, as on pencils
gin is a spirit

annotation.surface: A heavy drinker's spirits are coming back.
annotation.walkthrough: HGIN reads NIGH backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: An adjective synonym, a little old-fashioned: the end is nigh means it is approaching.
